The execution value restates iteration 17's finding in the two-dimension vocabulary (every published row read; the gap is the publisher's); it is not new coverage, and the 2025 file was verified by size and date header, not re-read.

lanes.source_family: NOAA National Hurricane Center Tropical Cyclone Reports (TCRs), read from NHC's own season indexes for the Atlantic and eastern Pacific basins, 2022-2026.
registry: NOAA National Hurricane Center summaries and Tropical Cyclone Reports
lanes.finding: The Arthur report documents rain, flooding and tornado damage in Texas, Louisiana and the Southeast but gives no outage count, shut-in volume or facility effect, so it yields no candidate. The execution value restates iteration 17's result in the two-dimension vocabulary.
lanes.limitation: NHC has not published reports for Atlantic Dolly, Edouard, Fay, Gonzalo, Hanna, Isaias and Josephine, nor for eastern-Pacific Douglas, Elida, Fausto, Karina, Lowell, Marie and the storms after Norbert. Of the four US-affecting storms that were unpublished on 2026-11-03, one (Arthur) is now out; Edouard, Isaias and Lowell are still unpublished. Josephine (21-22 Oct 2026) was not assessed for US effects because no search could be run.

registry: BSEE storm shut-in releases; EIA Today in Energy

lanes.finding: BSEE's Data Center (data.bsee.gov) answers ordinary requests where the newsroom does not, but it holds no storm statistics. Deriving shut-ins from its monthly production series would be an inference, not a reported effect, and was not attempted.

lanes.source_family: PHMSA pipeline enforcement raw data file (all Corrective Action Order cases)
registry: PHMSA incident data and corrective action orders
lanes.finding: PHMSA publishes no incident CSV, API or bulk file outside phmsa.dot.gov that is reachable by ordinary access. The primis enforcement site does publish an incident-linked case list, and it surfaced trunk-line shutdowns handled by safety order rather than corrective action order, a class the corrective-action-order census cannot see.
lanes.limitation: The incident data files, the only complete list of reportable pipeline incidents, are still unread: phmsa.dot.gov refuses the landing pages and the zip, and DOT's open-data portal only links back to them. A trunk-line shutdown that drew neither a corrective action order nor any other enforcement case is therefore invisible to this lane.

lanes.source_family: Per-terminal web query for unplanned LNG export terminal shutdowns
registry: US LNG terminal reporting (operators, EIA, FERC)
lanes.finding: Cameron, 2022-2026: the ten queries returned planned maintenance (2022, 2024, 2025, 2026) and one January 2024 freeze cargo cancellation with no reported train shutdown. One unverified lead remains: a search summary, with no attributable page, said all three Cameron trains shut unexpectedly on 2025-10-27; it is held, not accepted. Cove Point, 2022-2026: every plant shutdown the 10 queries surfaced is the scheduled autumn maintenance outage (excluded as planned), each year. The only unplanned items are a 14 June 2022 trip recorded in a PHMSA order with no stated effect, and a July 2023 feed gas reduction downstream of the Columbia Line VB rupture already in the corpus. A 2025 PHMSA proposed safety order on minor leaks states no shutdown. Result snippets from RBN and PipeRiv were not opened; RBN weekly reports are subscriber content.
lanes.limitation: Three of nine terminals were searched (Sabine Pass, Cameron, Cove Point); twelve queries for terminals not yet operating in the window were not applicable. The rest were not run because the search limit was reached.
